definitions.gloss: to lack, to be short of, to want for
definitions.explanation: To be in a state of not having enough of something. Most commonly used in the negative form 事欠かない, meaning "to have no shortage of" or "to never lack for."

examples.japanese: ⟦{話題|わだい}→話題：03793_wadai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{事欠|ことか}かない。
examples.english: There is no shortage of things to talk about.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの{人|ひと}→あの人：25922_anohito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{事欠|ことか}かない⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧だ。
examples.english: That person is someone who never runs out of problems.

examples.japanese: ⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧もの⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{事欠|ことか}くような⟦{生活|せいかつ}→生活：01443_seikatsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦していた→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あった→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There was a time when people lived lacking even food to eat.

notes:
USAGE:
{事欠|ことか}く is most frequently used in the negative form {事欠|ことか}かない, meaning "to have no shortage of" or "to never lack." The affirmative form {事欠|ことか}く (to lack) is rarer and sounds more literary.

The pattern ～⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{事欠|ことか}かない means "there is no shortage of ~."

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{事欠|ことか}かない: to have no shortage of
- ～⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{事欠|ことか}く: to lack even ~
- ⟦{話題|わだい}→話題：03793_wadai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{事欠|ことか}かない: never at a loss for topics
- ⟦{例|れい}→例：09932_rei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{事欠|ことか}かない: to have no shortage of examples
